extracted.intended_audience: policymakers and officials of the Unemployment Insurance Commission (UIC); legislative drafters; administrative law reformers; claimant-assistance agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommended standards for reorganizing Unemployment Insurance Act/Regulations procedural provisions, improving claimant information (publicity, form-letters, hearings), caselaw publication/indexing, access to files, and fact-finding practices for decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity obligation to inform insured persons and employers (proposed sec. 105A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal for a new sec. 105A: 'The Commission shall undertake such measures of publicity as it deems appropriate in order to inform insured persons and their employers of the provisions of this Act.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: make the public aware of the legal parameters of their actions. Note: the paper will later examine whether the UIC should also be required to inform claimants individually (beyond general publicity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reorganization, clarification and simplification of the Act and Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that consideration be given to 'a reorganization, clarification and simplification of the Act and Regulations', with emphasis on reorganizing procedural provisions to make texts more intelligible and directly usable by non-lawyers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: present drafting style and scattered Regulations make legal rules hard to understand and find. Scope limited here to procedural provisions; full statutory redrafting is outside study but procedural reorganization is feasible and recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and publication of an administrative consolidation (updated edition) of the Act and Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that the UIC prepare and publish an 'administrative consolidation' (updated edition) of the Act and Regulations for its own convenience and for employers and employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentation should be modest; price nominal; can appear as appendix to an information manual. Consolidation should include cross-references between main sections of the Act/Regulations and divisions of the manual. Even if legislation is later redrafted, an administrative consolidation is worthwhile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group all procedural provisions in a separate Part ('Claim Procedure')
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to group procedural provisions of most direct practical interest to claimants in a separate part of the Act (to be inserted between present Parts II and III) or, failing that, in the Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim: eliminate dispersal of procedural provisions that makes comprehension difficult. Transpose into the Act those Regulations that offer important safeguards or are useful for claimants, gather them under heading 'Claim Procedure'. Consider parliamentary sanction vs convenience of Regulations; if Regulations used, broaden Advisory Committee review powers to ensure prior scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include specified content areas in the new 'Claim Procedure' Part
rubrics_metrics.description: List of the procedural topics that 'should be included in this new Part of the Act'—namely: (1) Initial processing of claims; (2) Appeals to the Board of referees; (3) Appeals to the Tribunal; (4) Reexamination of decisions; (5) Benefit Control; (6) Overpayments; (7) Sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each item in the list references existing sections of the Act and Regulations (specific sections are enumerated in the text). The new Part should consolidate provisions most useful to claimants covering all stages of claim processing, including precontentious and contentious stages and procedural incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing of claims (to be set out in Act/Regulations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial processing stage of claims should be explicitly included in the consolidated procedure provisions (text lists relevant Act sections such as 20(4), 53 (amended), 54 (amended), 55 (amended), 57 (French version only), 105, 106, 107, 114 and Regulations 146(1)-(4), 149, 150(2)-(3), 160, 161).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: claimants need clear, accessible rules governing the first (and most immediate) stages of claims. If transposed into the Act, these provisions enjoy parliamentary sanction; if left in Regulations, ensure consultation mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to the Board of referees (procedural protections and clarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural provisions relating to appeals to the Board of referees should be consolidated (references include Act sec. 91 (amended subs.(5)), 94 and Regulations such as 178(4), 179 (with many new subss.), 180 (amended), 181 (new subs.(1)), 182 (new subs.(3) etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation should ensure clarity about appeal rights and processes and include safeguards currently in Regulations that are of particular use to claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to the Tribunal (comprehensive revision and transposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose comprehensive revision of Tribunal appeal provisions and transposition of certain Regulations into Act sections (e.g., revised secs. 92, 95, 96; amendments to 93, 97–103; incorporation of Reg. 167 into sec.103(2); revision of 184–186; creation of new sec.92A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: ensure that appellate-stage procedures are clear, accessible, and organized within the statutory scheme for claimant benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination of decisions (statutory procedure and notification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 102 of the Act should be amended (new subss.(2) and (3)) to clarify reexamination of decisions procedure and claimant notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation should define time limits and notification practices for reconsideration of claims so claimants are informed of changes affecting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit control (procedural placement and safeguards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit control provisions (currently secs. 113 and 115 of the Act) should be included in the consolidated procedural Part, with appropriate cross-references and safeguards for claimants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: benefit control procedures are a core part of claim processing and should be readily accessible to claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overpayments (clarity of rights and remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overpayments provisions (Act sections such as 49(3)-(4) amended, 50–52, 79 (new subs.(1)), 80 (new subs.(1)), 112; proposed new sec.49A; Reg.175 changes to become sec.49B) should be consolidated and clarified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: make rules on liability, calculation, and recovery of overpayments intelligible to claimants and officials alike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions (statutory clarity and placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions provisions (Act secs.47, 121–124, 128; proposed new sec.47A) should be included in the procedural Part to clarify punitive measures available and the circumstances in which they apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If placed in Regulations, ensure Advisory Committee review; consolidation aims to make the sanctions regime more transparent to claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign permanent legal translators to speed caselaw publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that two legal translators be permanently assigned to the Insurance Policy Branch to translate Umpire decisions promptly once a decision is selected for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: current publication delays largely due to translation lag. Translators could later serve a reorganized appeal tribunal. UIC already has an advance publication system for internal use; additional translators would reduce public publication delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a detailed, alphabetical, subject index to the Umpires' caselaw (bilingual, non-translated)
rubrics_metrics.description: An index of decisions is required: 'a detailed, alphabetical index by subject, which would require two separate versions in both official languages, since an index cannot be translated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority: highest. Implementation stages: (1) prepare and publish index of decisions since the 1971 reform (1971–1976); (2) selective index for applicable decisions from 1940–1971; (3) provide index for each new volume and publish cumulative index at regular intervals. Estimated one year of intensive work for 1971–1976 section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use caselaw index to improve Agent II, Board, and claimant practice and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of a reliable comprehensive index will enable Agents II to research caselaw independently, allow claimants and representatives to find supporting precedents, and help Boards of referees to evaluate parties' positions more critically and gain improved knowledge of caselaw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also useful for training Agents II and Board members; makes assimilation of essential rulings feasible by enabling quick searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and standardization of group information sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Group information sessions only valuable if used with 'a modicum of educational
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful attention to form and content; sessions should be presented by employees with knowledge of teaching methods and adequate material; standardized as far as possible; avoid presenting too much information, irrelevant detail, overly fast delivery, or threatening allusions to penalties. Only include signing by claimant if sessions demonstrably effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized explanations by Insurance Agents and unit-based service
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents should provide personalized service via the service-unit structure to establish direct contact with claimants; human qualities (interest, tact, patience, warmth) improve claimant understanding and acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents' training courses should stress the educational aspect of their work; administrative action requires cooperative fact-finding with claimants rather than judicial detachment. Routine impassiveness is sometimes wise but human warmth often reassures and increases claimant responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear warning about penalties (Agent duty)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents should inform claimants of dangers in failing to fulfil obligations (withholding of benefit, demands for reimbursement, garnishment, administrative penalties, prosecution) without needlessly arousing indignation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fair play is more important than tact: the UIC must not withhold information about penalties. Finding a way to warn claimants at the outset, in a non-alarmist way, is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory obligation to give reasons and notify claimants about how decisions may be changed (proposed amendments to secs.53,54,57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments: Sec.53(3) — require notification of decision 'together with the reasons therefor in the case of a decision against him.' Sec.54(2) and (3) — notify decision 'together with the reasons therefor in the case of a decision against him and information on the circumstances under which benefit may continue or cease to be payable.' Sec.57(1) — require notification of reconsideration decisions 'together with the reasons therefor in the case of a decision against him.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: introduce a fundamental administrative principle that the author of an administrative decision should notify affected persons of the reasons and advise them of consequences and how decisions may be amended. Textual amendments are quoted verbatim in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-letters must be clear, precise, legally accurate, and include specific factual/legal explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Form-letters are commonly used to notify claimants; the report finds clumsy phraseology, grammatical/syntactic errors, and imprecise use of legal/administrative terminology. Positive aspects: UIC usually advises claimant of right to provide additional information, right to appeal, and cites Act/Reg section in letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: improve clarity and legal terminology; include blank spaces in standardized forms (including those used for refusal/disentitlement) so Agent can indicate concrete factual and legal reasons; avoid multiple notices to same claimant on same day; develop multi-purpose forms for common situations; when citing a provision, explain it in everyday context rather than repeat text word-for-word.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit administrative secrecy—allow claimant access to file and disclose crucial sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Under sec.114 the UIC is sole judge of disclosing file contents; in practice claimants have fairly broad access when an appeal is lodged, but before litigation UIC does not normally reveal sources of leads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation: broaden claimant rights to view files; where information from a third party is a crucial factor and contradicted by the claimant, the UIC should not refuse to divulge the source. Clarify scope of sec.114 regarding administrative tribunals' power to compel production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized introductory statements by Board chairmen at hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Chairmen should open each hearing with a brief statement introducing Board members and their status, reminding claimant that members represent contributors and are independent of UIC, explaining purpose of hearing, and stressing informal/confidential nature of proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current practice varies; UIC should issue a circular letter reminding chairmen of obligations and providing a standard format listing points to be covered (including explanation of presence of clerk and tape recording). Longer-term measures to standardize Board chairman practices are proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker must have sufficient facts; gather by oral and written investigation and weight evidence appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle: 'the author of an administrative decision should have available sufficient information on the circumstances of the case he has to adjudicate.' Facts may be acquired by oral investigation (inquiring of those involved) or written investigation (documents). Before applying law, decision-maker weights items of information according to criteria derived from law but extraneous to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter is divided into gathering facts, documentation available, and assessment. Two points singled out for further discussion: benefit control and fact-finding by appeal bodies (Board of referees). The report emphasizes sufficiency of information and proper assessment procedures.
